analysis.title: The Hunt for Red October: Risks Shifting from RSP to SPY as Yields See Tactical Exhaustion
key_insights: October has been known as the 'Bear Killer', with bullish reversals ending bear markets in 2002, 2011 and 2022. Those October lows followed drawdowns of about 48%, 22% and 27%. The SPX is roughly flat since June and not far from all-time highs, so the setup differs.

9 of 11 sectors are down more than 2% over the last month, yet the 10-day averages of equity and composite put/call ratios are near the lows of the year. The Daily Sentiment Index for the VIX is 19%. Few investors are positioned for a high-correlation index volatility event, which BTIG says is why the risk of one in October is high.
30-year yields rose from 5.25% to 5.69% in 7 sessions and the Daily Sentiment Index for bonds is 10%. BTIG sees yields nearing tactical upside exhaustion and a risk of a quick snap-back lower.
If yields fall, the QQQ vs. IWM ratio and similar correlations may revert. Breadth could rebound from extremely oversold conditions, but lower rates could also push QQQ and the Mag7 lower.

RSP (equal-weight S&P 500) tactical risk/reward is no longer negative. BTIG's August 19 RSP/BKX study flagged many names within a week or two of a cyclical or tactical top, and that has largely played out. RSP is nearing its 200-day moving average.
BTIG sees much greater downside risk to SPY, QQQ and the Mag7 than to RSP.
Credit is still getting worse: the B vs. CCC spread hit a fresh wide through 7%.
